report.source_text: Her focal seizures progressed to prolonged, refractory status epilepticus, requiring intensive care unit (ICU) admission. Seizure control was established with multiple anti-seizure medications. Intravenous corticosteroids were also given to cover for potential immune-mediated seizure pathology. Appropriate investigations found no underlying cause for the epilepsy. Her seizures stabilised and she was stepped down from ICU to the general neurology ward.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old pregnant woman presented with focal impaired awareness seizures involving right upper limb and progression to bilateral tonic-clonic seizures at 18 weeks of pregnancy. EEG confirmed electroclinical status epilepticus and epilepsia partialis continua. Brain MRI showed abnormal cortical signals in the left parietal, posterolateral temporal and occipital lobes initially, later evolving to left thalamic gliotic scarring. CSF analysis was normal and negative for viral PCR and autoimmune encephalitis antibodies. Valproate was withdrawn due to suspicion of POLG mutation related hepatotoxicity risk. Clinical improvement occurred after ICU admission, corticosteroid and multi-agent anti-seizure treatment. Genetic testing was ordered but no direct report excerpt documenting the POLG biallelic compound heterozygous pathogenic variants was found in the provided records.
